draft.title: Types of settlement
card: A settlement is a place where people live, from a large city to a small community. Settlements differ in how many people live there and how far they are from services such as hospitals and shops.
Urban
a city or large town with many people living close together. Services are close by.
Rural
a town, farm or small community with fewer people, spread over more land. Larger centres with more services are within reach.
Remote and very remote
small communities a long way from larger centres. The further away a place is, the more remote it is called.
draft.remember: Settlement types depend on size and distance from services.

a.q: Which description best fits a remote community in Australia?
opts: Few people, far from larger centres and their services
Many people, close to a city and its services
Few people, but close to a city and its services
Many people, but far from larger centres and services
a.why: Remote communities are small and a long way from larger centres. A place with few people that is close to a city is not remote, because distance from services is what matters.
a.clue: Think about both size and distance.

b.q: Kiah lives on a farm in Tasmania. The nearest big town is 40 minutes away by car. Which type of settlement is this most likely to be?
opts: Rural, as it is small and spread out but within reach
Urban, because there is a town within driving distance
Very remote, because the nearest town is not next door
Urban, because farms are part of a city's settlement
b.why: A farm with a town 40 minutes away is rural. It has few people and some distance to services, but it is not far enough to be very remote. Having a town nearby does not make a farm urban.
b.clue: A farm is spread out, but the town is still within reach.

a.best: Few people, far from larger centres and their services

b.best: Rural, as it is small and spread out but within reach

problems.detail: The clue 'A farm is spread out, but the town is still within reach' repeats the wording of the right option ('spread out but within reach'). A student can match the words without knowing the idea.
